prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1019; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a left-turn collision at an intersection, with the other vehicle striking the driver's side as the insured was turning across oncoming traffic. The claimant's attorney has notified us of representation and asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the impact. The driver is named on the policy, and the coverage records show no gap in coverage around the loss.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who gave the same description of the collision as the insured did. Photos from the scene line up with that account and show the damage pattern we would expect from the impact.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses gave statements confirming the left turn and the point of impact. Neither had any connection to either party.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle and found damage largely consistent with the described impact. No earlier body damage or prior repairs were visible, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 6: Claimant reports a back strain from the collision. The injury fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type, and the claimant's account of symptoms has stayed the same in every contact so far.

Entry 7: Medical records show the claimant had a small strain in the same area several years ago, which resolved completely with care. The prior episode has no bearing on the current complaint as documented.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course for this kind of strain, with physical therapy and scheduled follow-up visits. Care has tapered as the claimant's condition has improved.

Entry 9: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the same account of the collision and the treatment timeline. Requested updated treatment notes to close out the medical file.

Entry 10: Reviewed all materials gathered to date. The loss appears to match the reported facts, and the file is ready for the next settlement review.
